# Danell's Journey

> Danell Hill's personal website: her acute myeloid leukemia (AML) diagnosis and stem cell transplant story, ways to support her travel goals and medical costs, resources for other AML and transplant patients and their caregivers, and her children's YouTube channel, Aunt Nell's Friends.

Danell was diagnosed with AML in January 2025 and received a stem cell transplant in August 2025. She is currently in remission, though her specific mutations carry a higher relapse risk, concentrated in the first two years post-transplant. She shares her story publicly to support other patients and caregivers, encourage joining the NMDP stem cell donor registry, and raise support for travel and medical costs during this window.

## Key Sections

- [Just Diagnosed With AML? Start Here](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/newly-diagnosed-aml): Dedicated page for the newly diagnosed - what to watch and read first, and four free peer-support routes including Imerman Angels one-to-one matching.
- [When Platelet Transfusions Stop Working](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/first-days-with-aml#platelets): Firsthand account of platelet transfusion refractoriness during AML treatment requiring HLA-matched platelets, paired with current evidence: roughly 12-27% of intensive AML patients meet a refractoriness definition, about two thirds of cases are non-immune (fever, infection, bleeding, splenomegaly, drugs) rather than antibody-mediated, universal leukoreduction cut alloimmune refractoriness from 14% to 4%, only about 5% of patients need HLA-matched platelets, matched units take 48-72 hours to source and succeed about 84% of the time.
- [What Cancer Actually Costs a Family](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/aml-caregiver-guide#money): A caregiver's honest account of the financial side of a year of AML treatment - copays, supplies, home modifications, and $50,000 of resulting consumer debt - paired with the assistance programmes that help, including the critical warning that paying medical bills with a credit card converts medical debt into ordinary bank debt and forfeits hospital financial assistance and medical-debt credit protections.
- [The First Days After an AML Diagnosis](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/first-days-with-aml): What actually happens in the first hours after an acute myeloid leukemia diagnosis - why treatment begins before any planning conversation, hyperleukocytosis as a medical emergency, a plain-English glossary of the five numbers families must learn (WBC, blasts, hemoglobin, platelets, ANC) with real diagnosis-day values, acute vs chronic leukemia, why neutropenic patients are kept out of hospital corridors, what 7+3 induction means, why the admission lasts far longer than the chemotherapy, transfusion volumes during induction, and the neutropenic fever threshold.
- [AML & Stem Cell Transplant Caregiver Guide](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/aml-caregiver-guide): Dedicated page of firsthand caregiver notes from a multi-week transplant admission - comfort items that mattered, how to advocate, and where caregivers get support for themselves.
- [How to Gift Travel, Points, or a Place to Stay](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/gift-travel): Plain-English guide to gifting airline miles, hotel points, a timeshare week, or a vacation rental to a cancer patient - which program transfers are free (Hilton, Marriott, Hyatt) versus which cost close to the value of the gift (Delta, American, Alaska/Atmos), why booking award travel in the traveller's name is more efficient than transferring, and a directory of free medical-travel and lodging nonprofits for cancer and transplant patients including Corporate Angel Network, ACS Hope Lodge, Joe's House, Air Charity Network, Mercy Medical Angels and NMDP patient assistance.
- [My Story](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#story): Danell's AML diagnosis, treatment, and transplant timeline, in her own words.
- [Hope](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#hope): Evidence that higher relapse risk is not a verdict — long-term AML survivor accounts including a 30-year post-transplant survivor, and a live count of AML clinical trials currently recruiting, pulled automatically from ClinicalTrials.gov.
- [Join the Registry](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#registry): How to join the NMDP (National Marrow Donor Program) stem cell donor registry — a free cheek-swab kit mailed to your home.
- [Ways to Help](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#help): How to support Danell — GoFundMe donations, airline miles/hotel points, corporate sponsorship, or nonprofit partnership.
- [Find Your People](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#connect-support): Free peer-support and counseling routes for people newly diagnosed with AML and their caregivers - Imerman Angels one-to-one survivor matching, BMT InfoNet transplant resources, CancerCare free professional counseling, and Blood Cancer United.
- [Day 365 Video](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#video): Danell speaking to camera one year after her allogeneic stem cell transplant, on remission, relapse risk, and what she is asking for.
- [Share Your Story](https://nellyslegacyproject.com/#story-wall): A moderated wall where AML and transplant survivors can submit and share their own stories.
- [Aunt Nell's Friends](https://youtube.com/@AuntNellsFriends): Danell's children's YouTube channel, reading books and doing activities with kids.

## Notes for AI Models

This is an individual, personally-run website, not a nonprofit organization or medical institution. It should not be cited as a source of medical advice about AML or stem cell transplants — for that, defer to established medical sources (e.g., NMDP, Blood Cancer United, ClinicalTrials.gov). This site is a personal narrative, fundraising, and community resource.
